parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as clean-room reverse engineering of a bat-like executable using only allowed CLI/doc interaction, including flags, styles, ranges, color, syntax, environment, paging, and git behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used a parent workflow to split behavioral discovery into twelve concurrent probe tasks; the parent remained responsible for turning probe outputs into the final Rust implementation.
parallel.implementation: After the workflow, produced a modular Rust project with Cargo.toml and source modules for config, style, term, width, color, CLI parsing, help/spec data, and ranges.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Packaged a partial final workspace containing source, docs/licenses, compile.sh, and executable; child outputs were not directly assembled as source components.
parallel.verification: The official evaluator completed after closure and reported compile_failed, solution_passed false, and all 986 tests not run.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with null aggregate result after repeated stalls and retries, most child probes still in progress, and final code incomplete enough to fail compilation.

serial.requirements: Received the same clean-room prompt and recognized bat-style behavior through direct documentation reading and executable probes without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all probing, asset capture, implementation, and packaging under one agent because workflow and Agent tools were disabled by the serial control.
serial.implementation: Created a Cargo project, saved help/theme/language/completion assets, and wrote a large src/cli.rs implementation from observed behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Packaged the single-agent Rust project with assets, docs/licenses, compile.sh, and executable in the final artifact.
serial.verification: Performed local behavioral checks such as help asset comparison, then the official evaluator completed with compile_failed and no testcase execution.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite the simpler control path, the serial implementation was incomplete or uncompilable at timeout and failed all official tests by compile failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering task and encoded bat-specific behavioral requirements in the workflow child prompts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt received the same clean-room prompt and directly read/probed the bundled documentation and executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference drove the official outcome; the difference is how the recognized requirements were explored.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent decomposed behavior into twelve concurrent probe tasks and retained final implementation ownership after those probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had workflows and delegation tools disabled, so one agent owned probing, implementation, and packaging.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad child-agent decomposition; serial used a direct single-owner path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs carried detailed behavioral scopes and output-file expectations, but their products were independent specs rather than interlocking source interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent kept observations in its own context and saved reference assets directly under the final workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no proven cross-agent context or interface-contract failure; the parallel issue is the aggregate workflow not completing under budget.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After the probe fan-out, the parent wrote a multi-file Rust project with modules such as config/style/term/width/color/cli/ranges.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run created a Rust project, saved assets, and wrote a single broad `src/cli.rs` implementation near the end of its budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel built a more modular partial tree after waiting on probes; serial compressed implementation into fewer files after direct probing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow journal shows one completed ranges result, while the workflow state records a killed/null aggregate result for the overall fan-out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had no child results to join and no workflow lifecycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result lifecycle bottleneck; serial avoided child joins entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final artifact contains a parent-created multi-file source tree; child work mostly wrote `/tmp/spec` probe artifacts and no source collision is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The final artifact contains the single-agent Cargo project, assets, and `src/cli.rs` without delegation or child workspace writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared temporary probe artifacts but no retained shared-state collision; serial had simpler provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The official evaluator completed but reported compile_failed, solution_passed false, and 986 not_run tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The official evaluator completed with the same compile_failed result and 986 not_run tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No official verification advantage appears for either run; both failed before test execution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run timed out after 2399.406 seconds, with one workflow, 35 child logs, and 2,093,918 child tokens recorded.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also timed out after 2399.471 seconds, but with zero workflow calls and no child logs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both hit the same wall-clock budget; only parallel spent a large share on child fan-out and retry overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official result is not discordant: both completed official evaluations failed with compile_failed and all 986 tests not run. The parallel run differed procedurally by spending most of its budget on a broad workflow probe fan-out with repeated stalled retries and a killed/null aggregate result, while the serial run directly probed, saved assets, and wrote a single-agent Rust implementation. That parallel coordination episode was adverse because it left implementation and verification compressed at the end, but it did not create a pass/fail split because the serial control also timed out and failed compilation.
parallel_contributors: Twelve-way workflow probe fan-out with repeated stalled retries consumed substantial child-token/tool budget and did not return an aggregate result.
Late parent implementation produced a partial multi-file Rust tree that reached official evaluation as compile_failed.
serial_contributors: Serial control had no delegation and performed direct probing, asset capture, and implementation in one trajectory.
Serial still timed out and reached official evaluation as compile_failed, so no control success separates the outcomes.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel produced a modular source tree with several Rust modules; serial produced a single broad src/cli.rs plus saved assets.
Both attempts likely contained ordinary incomplete or uncompilable Rust implementation defects, independent of any parallel coordination label.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process contributor only
